extracted.intended_audience: state agency rulewriters, administrative-law attorneys, legislators, and members of the public interested in Montana rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for adopting, publishing, filing, noticing, and litigating administrative rules and contested cases under the Montana Administrative Procedure Act (MAPA) and related practice guidance. Includes requirements for emergency rules, petitions, register/code publication, contested-case notice and records, and evidentiary rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviated notice under emergency conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: In many situations an agency will have time to give an abbreviated notice which will permit interested persons to have some input in the rule-making process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The attorney general's model rule 6 provides a form for abbreviated notice of rulemaking under emergency conditions, as suggested by McCrory. Agencies should use abbreviated notice when full notice is impracticable but some input is still feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity: substantial compliance and six-month limit
rubrics_metrics.description: No rule is valid unless adopted in substantial compliance with subsections (1) or (2) of this section and within 6 months of the publishing of notice thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The six-month limitation prevents reliance on stale notices; substantial compliance (rather than perfect procedural form) is required for validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of informal conferences, consultations, and advisory committees
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may use informal conferences and consultations as a means of obtaining the viewpoints and advice of interested persons... An agency may also appoint committees of experts or interested persons or representatives of the general public to advise it with respect to any contemplated rule making. The powers of the committees shall be advisory only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These techniques may be employed in addition to formal requirements; however, advisory committees do not relieve the agency from following the formal rule-making procedures required by MAPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnecessary repetition of statutory language
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules may not unnecessarily repeat statutory language. Whenever it is necessary to refer to statutory language in order to convey the meaning of a rule interpreting the language, the reference shall clearly indicate that portion of the language which is statutory and the portion which is amplification of the language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each rule shall include a citation of authority pursuant to which it, or any part thereof, is adopted. This prevents rules from simply restating statutes and requires clear attribution of statutory vs. interpretive text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual review of agency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall at least annually review its rules to determine if any new rule should be adopted or any existing rule should be modified or repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision responds to findings that many agencies go long periods without reviewing rules; agencies should maintain a schedule/process for periodic review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive rule authority and consistency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To be effective, each substantive rule adopted must be within the scope of authority conferred and in accordance with standards prescribed by other provisions of law. No rule adopted is valid or effective unless consistent and not in conflict with the statute and reasonably necessary to effectuate the purpose of the statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied statutory delegation supports only interpretive rules, while legislative rules require express delegation. Courts will invalidate rules inconsistent with authorizing statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing rules with Secretary of State; general effective-date rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall file with the secretary of state a copy of each rule adopted by it. Each rule shall become effective after publication in the Montana administrative register as provided in 82-4206, except that a later date required by statute or specified in the rule shall be the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normal effective date is the day following the stated publication date. The Secretary of State publishes format/style rules that specify timing details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency rule immediate effectiveness and required finding
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to applicable constitutional or statutory provisions, an emergency rule shall become effective immediately upon filing with the secretary of state or at a stated date following publication ... if the agency finds that this effective date is necessary because of imminent peril to the public health, safety, or welfare. The agency's finding and a brief statement of reasons therefor shall be filed with the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must take appropriate measures to make emergency rules known to every person who may be affected by them; emergency rules are exceptional and require documented reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of State format, refusal, and public register duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The secretary of state may prescribe a format, style, and arrangement for rules ... and may refuse to accept the filing of any rule that is not in compliance therewith. He shall keep and maintain a permanent register of all rules filed ... which shall be open to public inspection, and shall provide copies of any rule upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary may require payment of copying costs; uniform format aids administration and public access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of administrative code: compilation, indexing, correction
rubrics_metrics.description: The secretary of state shall compile, index, arrange, rearrange, correct errors or inconsistencies without changing the meaning, intent, or effect of any rule, and publish all rules filed pursuant to this part in a publication known as the administrative rules of Montana (the code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary may include editorial notes and cross-references and publish supplements or revisions as necessary; corrections must not change rule meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Montana Administrative Register: sections and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The register shall contain three sections, a rules section, a notice section, and an interpretation section. The rules section shall contain all rules filed since the preceding issue together with the concise statement of reasons required under 82-4204(1)(b). The notice section shall contain all rule-making notices filed ... The interpretation section shall contain all opinions of the attorney general and all declaratory rulings of agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each issue shall carry issue number/date and table of contents; pages must show issue number/date; register may include info to relate to the code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference and omitting bulky rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The secretary of state, with the consent of the adopting agency, may omit from the code or register any rule the publication of which would be unduly cumbersome, expensive, or otherwise inexpedient, if the rule merely incorporates by reference a model code, federal agency rule, or like publication made available on application to the agency and if the code or register contains a notice stating the citation and general subject matter of the omitted rule and stating how a copy may be obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporation by reference should be limited to federal rules, model codes, or similar publications (i.e., materials not originating in Montana); agencies should provide information on how to obtain the omitted material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate publication and agency-paid copies
rubrics_metrics.description: The code shall be arranged, indexed, and printed or duplicated in such manner as to permit separate publication of portions thereof relating to individual agencies. An agency may make arrangements with the secretary of state for the printing of as many copies of such separate publications as it may require. The cost of any such separate publications shall be paid by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows agencies to maintain and distribute their own title-specific rule collections while central code remains authoritative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory free distribution list and retention requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The secretary of state shall distribute copies of the code and supplements or revisions thereto without charge to [specified public officers and institutions: attorney general; clerks of courts; county clerks; state law library; university units; legislative council; Library of Congress; state library; etc.]. The listed officers and librarians shall maintain a complete, current set of the code including supplements and the register issues published during the preceding 2 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated public offices must preserve current rule sets and registers to ensure public access; distribution list was revised by 1977 amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and pricing of copies and subscriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The secretary of state shall make copies of and subscriptions to the code and supplements or revisions thereto and the register available to any person at prices fixed to cover publication and mailing costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary will set subscription fees in consultation with the administrative code committee; fees cover costs but distribution to certain offices remains free.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees: cost determination, frequency of register, deposit of fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The secretary of state shall determine the cost of supplying copies ... Such cost shall be the approximate cost of printing or duplication and mailing. The secretary shall publish all notices, rules, and interpretations filed with him, at least once a month ... but not more often than twice a month, in a publication called the Montana administrative code register. The secretary shall deposit all fees he collects in the general fund. The secretary may charge agencies a filing fee for material to be published based on estimated printing costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical publication frequency may vary; advisory committee consults on fees; drafting errors created some tension between title/frequency provisions — practice governs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for adoption, amendment or repeal of rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An interested person or, when the legislature is not in session, a member of the legislature on behalf of an interested person may petition an agency requesting the promulgation, amendment, or repeal of a rule. Each agency shall prescribe by rule the form for petitions and the procedure for their submission, consideration, and disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within 60 days after submission the agency shall either deny the petition in writing (stating reasons) or initiate rulemaking proceedings in accordance with 82-4204. If rejected, the petitioner's remedy lies with the legislature; agencies may notice changes as petitioned or propose their own conforming/modifying changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial notice of filed and published rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The courts shall take judicial notice of any rule filed and published under the provisions of this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing and publication eliminate need for parties to prove existence/authenticity of rules in court; adopted into evidence rules (e.g., Mont. Rules of Evidence Rule 202(b)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contested-case notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In a contested case, all parties shall be afforded an opportunity for hearing after reasonable notice. The notice shall include: (a) a statement of the time, place and nature of the hearing; (b) a statement of the legal authority and jurisdiction under which the hearing is to be held; (c) a reference to the particular sections of the statutes and rules involved; (d) a short and plain statement of the matters asserted. If unable to state matters in detail, initial notice may be limited to a statement of the issues involved; thereafter a more definite statement shall be furnished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: What constitutes 'reasonable' notice varies by agency and context; the moment of notice may mark the beginning of contested-case protections (e.g., ban on ex parte communications). Forms and model rules (Attorney General's model rule 8, form 14) provide templates; sample motions and consent-order forms are provided in appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to present and informal disposition in contested cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Opportunity shall be afforded all parties to respond and present evidence and argument on all issues involved. Unless precluded by law, informal disposition may be made of any contested case by stipulation, agreed settlement, consent order, or default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should allow parties to respond to all evidence; informal resolution mechanisms are allowed where lawful (model forms exist).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record contents in contested case
rubrics_metrics.description: The record in a contested case shall include: (a) all pleadings, motions, intermediate rulings; (b) all evidence received or considered, including a stenographic record of oral proceedings when demanded by a party; (c) a statement of matters officially noticed; (d) questions and offers of proof, objections, and rulings thereon; (e) proposed findings and exceptions; (f) any decision, opinion or report by the hearing examiner or agency member presiding at the hearing; (g) all staff memoranda or data submitted to the hearing examiner or members of the agency as evidence in connection with their consideration of the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stenographic record must be transcribed on request; requesting party pays transcription costs unless statute provides otherwise. Findings of fact must be based exclusively on the evidence and matters officially noticed; staff legal memoranda prepared for decisionmakers are excluded from 'as evidence' unless submitted as evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcription and cost of stenographic records
rubrics_metrics.description: The stenographic record of oral proceedings or any part thereof shall be transcribed on request of any party. Unless otherwise provided by statute, the cost of the transcription shall be paid by the requesting party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: District courts have enforced transcription orders when appropriate; parties should be aware of cost allocation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findings of fact limited to record and official notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings of facts shall be based exclusively on the evidence and on matters officially noticed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due process requires decisionmakers' findings be grounded only in the hearing record; parties must be afforded opportunity to respond to all evidence that may be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies bound by common law and statutory rules of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided by statute relating directly to an agency, agencies shall be bound by common law and statutory rules of evidence. Objections to evidentiary offers may be made and shall be noted in the record. When a hearing will be expedited and the interests of the parties will not be prejudiced substantially, any part of the evidence may be received in written form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentary evidence may be received as copies/excerpts if originals not readily available; upon request parties shall be given opportunity to compare copy with original. Agencies must preserve right to require originals in appropriate cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to cross-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A party shall have the right to conduct cross-examinations required for a full and true disclosure of facts, including the right to cross-examine the author of any document prepared by or on behalf of or for the use of the agency and offered in evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-examination extends to agency-authored documents; agencies should anticipate and provide for witnesses/authors to be available when such documents are admitted.
